hypothesis: Multi-agent agentic AI systems, already demonstrated to autonomously optimize drug candidates through iterative closed-loop cycles, could be extended to autonomously design and adapt clinical trial protocols in real time—dynamically adjusting patient stratification, endpoints, and dosing arms based on accumulating trial data. Such a system would represent a qualitative leap from current AI-assisted trial outcome prediction toward a fully autonomous clinical trial co-investigator, potentially compressing the seven-plus-year drug development timeline by enabling continuous, evidence-driven protocol refinement without waiting for pre-specified interim analyses.

reasoning: PharmAgents demonstrates that multi-agent LLM systems can autonomously iterate over complex design decisions in drug development using closed-loop feedback (chunk 03-pharmagents:7), while biomedical foundation models already predict trial outcomes and simulate hypothetical scenarios to support trial design (chunk 02-biomed-fm:11). Combining these two capabilities suggests that an agentic system could close the loop further—not just predicting trial outcomes but continuously re-designing the trial itself in response to accumulating evidence, a step not yet described in any retrieved source.
